column3: The Hebrew describes them passively as “being struck before us”; BSB changes this to active “We are defeating them.”
The Hebrew leaves the subject of not knowing unnamed; BSB explicitly supplies “the Benjamites.” It describes the battle as “heavy,” rendered “fierce” in BSB.
The Hebrew describes the men as drawing a sword; BSB says they were “armed with swords.”
The Hebrew repeats “the ambush” as the subject of advancing; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “they.” Its sword expression literally says “the mouth of the sword.”
The Hebrew emphatically repeats the defeat root in the Benjamites’ statement; BSB has the single “are defeated.”
The Hebrew explicitly says that the whole city went up “toward heaven”; BSB says it went “up in smoke.”
The Hebrew uses collective singular “man of Israel” and “man of Benjamin,” with singular pronouns for Benjamin; BSB uses plural “men” and “they.”
The Hebrew explicitly describes treading Benjamin down; BSB replaces this with easily overtaking them. The east is expressed as the rising of the sun.
The Hebrew leaves the pursuing subject unnamed, where BSB supplies “Israel.” It describes the taking of five thousand with a gleaning image, which BSB renders as “cut down.”
The Hebrew repeats “the rock of Rimmon” as the place where they stayed; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “where.”
The Hebrew has no separate adjective corresponding to BSB’s “other Benjamites.” It calls the cities “found,” where BSB says “in their path.”
